name: Workato
short_description: Enterprise iPaaS that connects apps, data, workflows and AI agents with central governance.
long_description: Workato is an enterprise integration and automation platform. It connects business applications and data, runs automated workflows called recipes, and hosts AI agents, with governance controls for IT. The product range covers enterprise iPaaS, embedded integrations and API management. The pricing page lists platform editions starting with Standard, combined with a usage-based consumption component, and directs buyers to schedule a demo; it shows no public prices. Pricing and plan structures can vary with contract terms.
use_cases: Connect SaaS apps across departments;Automate IT and HR processes;Govern AI agents
use_case: Connect enterprise systems such as CRM, ERP and HR apps with recipes that sync data and run cross-department processes, and run governed AI agents on the same platform.
why_choose: It covers enterprise iPaaS, embedded integrations and API management in one platform, with recipe lifecycle management and separate dev, test and production environments.
how_to_start: No public self-serve plan: schedule a demo through the pricing page and choose a platform edition, starting with Standard. Workato offers training packages for building and managing recipes.

name: Tray.ai
short_description: AI-native enterprise iPaaS for building AI agents, governing MCP and integrating 700+ apps.
long_description: Tray.ai is an integration and automation platform for enterprises. Teams build integrations, automations and AI agents across more than 700 connected apps, and the platform includes governance for Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. The pricing page states that Tray starts at $50 a month, with usage settled at a true-up and volume discounts at larger scale. A 30-day free trial is available without a card or sales call. Premium support with a dedicated Slack channel is an upgrade.
use_cases: Integrate enterprise apps;Build governed AI agents;Manage MCP access
use_case: Integrate enterprise apps and build AI agents that act across more than 700 connected apps, with governance over which MCP servers agents can use.
why_choose: It combines a low-code drag-and-drop builder with headless use from Claude Code, Codex and MCP, and it publishes a starting price of $50/mo, which enterprise iPaaS vendors often do not.
how_to_start: Start the 30-day free trial, which needs no card or sales call, and build from a prebuilt template in the drag-and-drop builder. The trial helps size usage before buying.

name: UiPath
short_description: Platform for business orchestration and automation that combines RPA robots, AI agents and people.
long_description: UiPath is an automation platform built around robotic process automation (RPA), with AI agents and process orchestration through its Maestro product. Software robots carry out repetitive tasks in desktop and web applications, while agents and people handle steps that need judgment. The pricing page lists a free-forever plan, a Basic plan starting at $25 per month, and Standard and Enterprise plans with pricing from sales. Some plans offer a 60-day free trial. Deployment is cloud-hosted in several regions or on-premises.
use_cases: Automate repetitive desktop tasks;Orchestrate agents and robots;Process documents
use_case: Use software robots to repeat desktop and web tasks such as data entry across applications, and orchestrate AI agents, robots and people in one business process with Maestro.
why_choose: It is an established RPA platform that adds agents and orchestration, can be deployed in the cloud or on-premises, and has a free-forever plan.
how_to_start: Choose Try UiPath free to open the free-forever plan. The UiPath Academy, documentation and community forum cover first automations. Basic starts at $25/mo, and some plans have a 60-day trial.

name: Automation Anywhere
short_description: Agentic process automation system combining AI, automation and RPA for enterprise processes.
long_description: Automation Anywhere sells an agentic process automation system that combines AI agents, workflow automation and robotic process automation (RPA) for end-to-end business processes in large organisations. The site directs buyers to its sales team for pricing. A free Cloud Community Edition is offered to entrepreneurs, developers, students and small businesses. The company also runs a learning platform, Automation Anywhere University, and a developer community called Pathfinder.
use_cases: Automate finance and back-office processes;Deploy RPA bots;Coordinate agents across systems
use_case: Automate back-office processes end to end by combining RPA bots, document automation and AI agents across business systems.
why_choose: It targets mission-critical enterprise processes, and its product range includes process discovery, document automation and a CoE manager alongside RPA.
how_to_start: Get the free Cloud Community Edition, which the vendor offers to entrepreneurs, developers, students and small businesses. For company deployments, contact sales.

name: Pabbly Connect
short_description: No-code integration tool that moves data between apps and automates repetitive tasks.
long_description: Pabbly Connect is a no-code tool that links web applications so that an event in one app triggers actions in others. It is aimed at users without coding skills, and the vendor states that all features are included in its Basic plan. Internal steps are not counted as tasks. The pricing page shows $16 per month for 10,000 tasks, billed annually, and also lists a one-time lifetime-access plan. Pabbly Connect is part of the Pabbly suite of business apps.
use_cases: Sync data between apps;Automate lead routing;Send notifications from form submissions
use_case: Send data from one app to another when an event happens, for example passing a form submission to a CRM and an email tool, using instant webhooks and built-in formatters.
why_choose: The vendor states that all features are included in the Basic plan and that internal steps do not count as tasks. It also sells a one-time lifetime plan, unlike recurring-only competitors.
how_to_start: Sign up on the site, connect a trigger app or an instant webhook, then add action steps. Plans are priced by monthly tasks, from $16/mo for 10,000 tasks billed annually.

name: Albato
short_description: No-code automation platform with 1,000+ integrations and a white-label embedded iPaaS option.
long_description: Albato is a no-code platform for connecting apps and automating workflows, with more than 1,000 native integrations. A white-label embedded edition lets software companies offer integrations to their own users and AI agents without building them in-house. The pricing page lists a free plan with 100 transactions, Pro at $15 per month billed annually ($22 monthly) with a 7-day trial, and a Teams plan for agencies starting at $65 per month billed annually. Extra transactions cost $0.033 each.
use_cases: Connect marketing and CRM apps;Embed integrations in a SaaS product;Automate agency workflows
use_case: Automate data flows between marketing, CRM and sales apps, or embed white-label integrations and AI agents connected to 1,000+ apps inside a SaaS product.
why_choose: It serves end users and also SaaS vendors that want a white-label embedded iPaaS with an MCP server, so they do not have to build OAuth integrations themselves.
how_to_start: Start on the free plan (100 transactions) or the 7-day Pro trial and connect two apps. SaaS companies wanting the embedded version book a demo.

name: Integrately
short_description: No-code integration tool with ready-made one-click automations for 1,500+ apps.
long_description: Integrately is a no-code tool for connecting apps. It offers a library of ready-made automations that users activate in a few clicks instead of building workflows from scratch. It supports more than 1,500 apps, with webhooks, branching and scheduling. The pricing page lists a free plan with 100 tasks, Starter at $19.99 per month billed annually (2,000 tasks), Professional at $39, Growth at $99 and Business at $239 per month. Paid plans include live chat support.
use_cases: Activate prebuilt app integrations;Automate CRM and email updates;Sync e-commerce orders
use_case: Activate prebuilt automations between apps such as Calendly, Pipedrive, MailerLite or Freshdesk without designing the workflow yourself.
why_choose: Its focus is a library of ready-made one-click automations aimed at non-technical users, with live chat support on all paid plans.
how_to_start: Choose Get Integrately Free (100 tasks), search for your two apps and activate one of the suggested ready automations.

name: Latenode
price_from: Free tier; then from $0.00012 per CPU-second
short_description: AI workflow automation platform with built-in LLMs, 5,500+ integrations and usage-based pricing.
long_description: Latenode is a workflow automation platform where large language models are available inside workflow nodes without separate API keys; the vendor lists more than 335 models. Users build workflows and AI agents that connect to more than 5,500 integrations, and can add custom code. Pricing is based on execution time rather than on operations. A free plan with no credit card includes a monthly allowance of free compute, and additional runtime is billed from $0.00012 per CPU-second, with lower rates at higher volumes.
use_cases: Build AI agents connected to apps;Automate data enrichment with LLMs;Replace per-task automation pricing
use_case: Build workflows that call an LLM inside any node, for example to classify or enrich records, and connect them to 5,500+ apps or to agents through MCP.
why_choose: It charges for CPU execution time instead of per operation, includes access to 335+ LLMs without separate API keys, and allows JavaScript in any node.
how_to_start: Start on the free plan, which needs no card and includes a monthly compute allowance. Begin from a ready-made template on the drag-and-drop canvas.

name: Prowork by Parabola
short_description: AI workspace from Parabola that answers questions, builds reports and runs business processes.
long_description: Prowork is Parabola's AI workspace for operations work. It answers questions, builds reports and runs recurring processes. Users describe a task in plain language to its agent builder, and can inspect the data and logic at each step and edit any calculation. The pricing page lists self-serve plans with a free tier that can be used indefinitely, and Business plans with custom credit volumes, proof-of-concept onboarding and a dedicated account manager. Self-serve prices were not readable on the page.
use_cases: Automate operations reporting;Process order and inventory data;Run recurring spreadsheet workflows
use_case: Describe an operations task in plain language, such as reconciling inventory across Shopify, NetSuite and ShipHero by SKU, and let the agent build and run the process.
why_choose: Users can inspect the data and logic at every step and change any calculation, so results stay auditable.
how_to_start: Choose Start for free on the self-serve free tier and try a sample flow built on the provided datasets, such as Shopify inventory. Business customers start with a proof of concept.

name: Tines
short_description: Platform for building AI agents, apps and workflows on sensitive systems, with security governance.
long_description: Tines is a workflow platform for running automation and AI agents on sensitive systems, data and processes, with security and governance controls. It started in security operations and is now used across IT and other teams. The pricing page lists a free edition with unlimited users, spaces and connectors, 3 live workflows and a one-time $50 AI allowance. Paid editions for organisation-wide use are sold through the sales team. A community and examples gallery are available.
use_cases: Automate security alert triage;Run IT service workflows;Deploy governed AI agents
use_case: Automate security and IT work such as alert triage and incident handling, and run AI agents on sensitive systems under governance controls.
why_choose: It is built for sensitive systems and data, with security and governance controls, and the free edition allows unlimited users and connectors.
how_to_start: Sign up for the free edition (3 live workflows, a one-time $50 AI allowance) and start from the templates library or the five-minute flows.

name: Windmill
short_description: Open-source, code-first platform for scripts, workflows, internal apps and AI agents.
long_description: Windmill is an open-source developer platform for writing scripts, workflows, internal apps, AI agents and data pipelines in code or with AI assistance. It runs on a self-hostable orchestrator. Engineers keep control of what is deployed through features such as versioning. The pricing page lists a free open-source self-hosted edition with unlimited executions, a cloud plan priced at $170 per month for one builder, and a self-hosted Enterprise edition from $120 per month. A nonprofit plan is also available.
use_cases: Schedule scripts and data pipelines;Build internal tools on workflows;Self-host automation
use_case: Turn scripts into scheduled jobs, multi-step workflows, internal apps or data pipelines, and deploy them with versioning and git sync to GitHub or GitLab.
why_choose: It is open source and code-first, can be self-hosted with unlimited executions for free, and publishes its pricing.
how_to_start: Self-host with Docker or Kubernetes, or install the CLI (npm install -g windmill-cli), or use Windmill Cloud. Write a first script and promote it to a workflow.

name: Kestra
short_description: Open-source declarative orchestration platform for data, infrastructure and business workflows.
long_description: Kestra is an open-source orchestration platform where workflows are defined declaratively in YAML. It is used for data pipelines, infrastructure jobs and business processes, and offers more than 2,300 plugins. The open-source edition includes unlimited flows and executions. Kestra Cloud, a fully managed service, and Kestra Enterprise, which adds governance, multi-cloud and air-gapped deployment and support with an SLA, are sold through the sales team on an annual per-instance subscription. Customers cited on the site include teams that moved from Apache Airflow.
use_cases: Orchestrate data pipelines;Schedule infrastructure jobs;Replace Airflow DAGs
use_case: Orchestrate data pipelines, infrastructure jobs and business processes defined as declarative YAML, using 2,300+ plugins.
why_choose: Its workflows are declarative YAML, and the open-source edition includes unlimited flows and executions. Customer stories on the site describe moving from Airflow.
how_to_start: Choose Get Started to run the open-source edition, then adapt a ready-made Blueprint from the docs. Managed Cloud and Enterprise are sold through sales.

name: Node-RED
short_description: Open-source low-code tool for building event-driven flows in a browser editor.
long_description: Node-RED is an open-source low-code tool for event-driven applications. Users connect nodes in a browser-based flow editor to collect, transform and visualise data, and it runs on Node.js. It is used for home automation, industrial control systems and connecting APIs and devices. IBM's Emerging Technology Services team originally built it, and it is now a project of the OpenJS Foundation. FlowFuse, Inc., founded by its creator, offers commercial hosting. The current version is 5.0.9.
use_cases: Automate smart-home devices;Connect IoT sensors to dashboards;Wire APIs together
use_case: Wire devices, APIs and online services together in a browser-based flow editor, for example to collect sensor data and show it on a dashboard or to automate a smart home.
why_choose: It is free and open source under the OpenJS Foundation and is light enough to run on low-cost hardware such as a Raspberry Pi as well as in the cloud.
how_to_start: Install it locally with npm (Node.js), run it in Docker or on a Raspberry Pi, open the browser editor and import a flow from the community flow library.

name: Axiom.ai
short_description: Browser automation and web scraping tool usable with no code, via an API or through Claude.
long_description: Axiom.ai automates actions on websites, such as clicking, form filling and data extraction. Bots are built with a no-code Chrome extension, through a browser automation API, or by describing the task to Claude. Bots run in Axiom's cloud or on the user's own machine. Pricing is based on monthly runtime: Starter costs $15 per month for 5 hours, Pro $50 for 30 hours, Pro Max $150 for 100 hours and Ultimate $250 for 250 hours. Each plan offers a free trial, and desktop runs have no concurrency limit.
use_cases: Scrape website data into sheets;Automate form filling;Run repetitive web tasks
use_case: Automate repetitive website tasks such as scraping data into a spreadsheet, filling forms or clicking through pages, without code.
why_choose: Bots can be built in a no-code Chrome extension, through an API, or by describing them to Claude, and they run in the cloud or on your own machine. Desktop runs have no concurrency limit.
how_to_start: Install the Chrome extension, build a bot step by step or with AI, and run it on the free trial runtime. Starter costs $15/mo for 5 hours.

name: n8n
short_description: Workflow automation platform combining AI agents and integrations.
long_description: n8n is a workflow automation platform that combines AI agents with hundreds of app integrations and custom code, giving technical teams the flexibility of code with the speed of no-code. Its differentiator is that it can be self-hosted (free Community Edition) as well as used in the cloud. Cloud plans come with a free trial.
use_cases: Build multi-step app integrations;Run AI agents in workflows;Self-host automation
use_case: Build multi-step workflows that combine 500+ native integrations, any HTTP API, custom code and AI agents, for example routing leads or running an AI agent on incoming tickets.
why_choose: It can be self-hosted (free Community Edition, Docker or on-prem) to keep data in your environment, and it mixes visual nodes with code.
how_to_start: Self-host with Docker, or start an n8n Cloud free trial (no card). Begin from a workflow template, which every plan includes.

name: Zapier
short_description: No-code automation platform connecting 9,000+ apps with Zaps, tables, forms and AI agents.
long_description: Zapier is a no-code automation platform that connects more than 9,000 apps. Users build Zaps, which are trigger-and-action workflows that can have multiple steps, and can add Tables, Forms, AI agents and a Copilot assistant that drafts workflows from plain-language descriptions. The pricing page lists a Free plan at $0 per month, Professional from $19.99 per month and Team from $69 per month. Enterprise pricing comes from sales and adds unlimited users and admin controls.
use_cases: Connect apps without code;Automate lead and CRM updates;Build AI agents and tables
use_case: Connect apps with trigger-and-action Zaps, for example sending new form leads to a CRM and Slack, and add tables, forms and AI agents.
why_choose: It has the largest stated app library here (9,000+ apps and 66,000+ triggers and actions), plus Copilot, which drafts workflows from plain language.
how_to_start: Sign up for the Free plan, start from a template or describe the Zap to Copilot, choose a trigger and an action, test it and turn it on.

name: Make
short_description: Visual no-code platform for building automations and AI agent workflows across apps.
long_description: Make is a no-code automation platform where users build workflows, called scenarios, on a visual canvas that connects thousands of apps. It also supports AI agents that run inside those workflows. Usage is measured in credits. A free plan includes 1,000 credits per month, and paid plans add more credits and features; enterprise plans include 24/7 support.
use_cases: Build visual multi-step scenarios;Sync data between apps;Automate marketing ops
use_case: Build visual multi-step scenarios that move and transform data between apps, with AI agents running inside the scenario.
why_choose: Its visual canvas shows branching scenarios, and usage is measured in credits rather than per-Zap tasks.
how_to_start: Start on the free plan (1,000 credits/mo), build a first scenario on the canvas from the integration library, then add an AI agent if needed.

name: Activepieces
short_description: Open-source automation workspace with chat, agents, flows and tables connecting to 760+ apps.
long_description: Activepieces combines workflow automation, AI agents, chat and data tables in one workspace with more than 760 app connectors and an MCP server. Its core is open source and can be self-hosted. The hosted Free plan needs no card; Plus costs a flat $20 per month with ten times the free usage and pay-as-you-go beyond that, and Team costs $200 per month. Enterprise features include audit logs and embedding.
use_cases: Automate app integrations;Self-host workflows;Build AI agents
use_case: Automate workflows across 760+ app connectors, with AI agents, chat and data tables in one workspace, and expose the tools to agents through its MCP server.
why_choose: The core is open source and can be self-hosted. The hosted Plus plan is a flat $20/mo.
how_to_start: Use the hosted Free plan (no card) or self-host the open-source core, then connect apps and build a first flow.

name: Pipedream
short_description: Developer platform providing managed auth and thousands of API tools for agents and apps.
long_description: Pipedream gives developers managed authentication and more than 10,000 prebuilt tools across over 3,000 APIs, through its Connect product, so agents and apps can act in users' accounts. Conduit is a gateway for governing the AI tools a company uses. Building is free, with no card required; paid plans apply when integrations go into production, starting with the Startup plan at $99 per month on annual billing.
use_cases: Give agents authenticated API tools;Code-level workflows;Event-driven integrations
use_case: Give AI agents and apps authenticated actions in users' accounts across 3,000+ APIs, or build code-level, event-driven integrations.
why_choose: It is developer-focused, with managed authentication and 10,000+ prebuilt tools through Connect, plus Conduit for governing AI tools.
how_to_start: Start building for free with no card. Paid plans apply when integrations go into production, from $99/mo on annual billing.

name: IFTTT
short_description: No-code service linking 1,000+ apps and devices through simple trigger-action applets.
long_description: IFTTT connects more than 1,000 services, including Google apps, webhooks, Discord, Slack and smart home devices, through applets that run an action when a trigger fires. It is aimed at individuals and small businesses rather than complex enterprise workflows. A free plan allows using published applets; paid tiers start at $2.99 per month billed annually and $8.99 per month for multi-step and filter features.
use_cases: Link smart-home devices;Automate social posts;Personal app automations
use_case: Link 1,000+ services and smart-home devices with simple applets, for example posting to Discord or Slack when a trigger fires.
why_choose: It is a low-cost way for individuals and small businesses to set up simple trigger-action automations, from $2.99/mo.
how_to_start: Choose Get started, enable a published applet on the free plan, or build your own with a trigger and an action.

name: Microsoft Power Automate
short_description: Microsoft's cloud and desktop automation service with RPA and Copilot features.
long_description: Power Automate is part of Microsoft Power Platform. It automates workflows across cloud apps, systems and websites, and includes robotic process automation for desktop tasks, process mining and Copilot-assisted flow creation. A 30-day free trial is available. The Premium plan costs $15 per user per month paid yearly; Process and Hosted Process licences for unattended bots cost $150 and $215 per bot per month.
use_cases: Automate Microsoft 365 processes;Desktop RPA;Approval flows
use_case: Automate approvals and workflows across Microsoft 365 and cloud apps, and automate desktop tasks with RPA bots.
why_choose: It is part of Microsoft Power Platform and includes desktop RPA, process mining and Copilot-assisted flow creation.
how_to_start: Start the 30-day trial or sign in with a Microsoft account, then describe a cloud flow to Copilot.

name: Gumloop
short_description: No-code builder for AI agents and workflows that connect to company tools and models.
long_description: Gumloop is a builder for AI agents and automations that non-engineers can use. Users combine AI models with integrations to apps such as Slack, Gmail and CRMs, then share the agents across the company while IT controls access. Templates cover sales research, outbound writing and customer success tasks. The pricing page lists Pro from $37 per month with a 14-day free trial, and Enterprise at custom pricing; no free plan was listed.
use_cases: Build AI agents connected to company tools;Automate sales research;Customer success workflows
use_case: Build AI agents for tasks such as account research, outbound writing or customer success, connected to Slack, Gmail and CRMs.
why_choose: It is aimed at non-engineers, and agents can be shared across the company while IT controls access.
how_to_start: Choose Get Started (Pro has a 14-day trial; no free plan was listed) and open a task template such as Account Researcher.

name: Lindy
short_description: Build AI agents that automate work across your tools.
long_description: Lindy lets individuals and teams create AI agents that connect to their apps and company knowledge. The agents handle email, scheduling, sales follow-ups and similar tasks, and they are built without code. New users get $50 in free credits, valid for 7 days, with no card required. The Team plan starts at $49.99 per month for 5,000 credits, and larger credit packs cost more. Lindy's own marketing calls its agents AI employees.
use_cases: Delegate email and meeting tasks;Automate follow-ups;Team AI assistant
use_case: Delegate email, scheduling and sales follow-ups to AI agents connected to Gmail, Slack, Notion, HubSpot and 1,500+ tools, or put repeated work on a schedule.
why_choose: Agents are built without code and can be reached in Slack, iMessage or email.
how_to_start: Try it free with $50 in credits (valid 7 days, no card), connect your tools and ask it to do a task.

name: Relevance AI
price_from: The official pricing page shows only an Enterprise plan, with pricing on request.
short_description: Platform for building and running AI agents for sales, support, marketing and HR tasks.
long_description: Relevance AI is a platform for building and operating AI agents that carry out business tasks such as research, outreach, qualification and support. Teams can configure specialist agents, connect them to their tools and run them at scale. Its Invent assistant helps identify processes to automate and turns them into agents. The pricing page showed only an enterprise offer during this check, so no price was recorded.
use_cases: Build sales and support AI agents;Automate HR workflows
use_case: Configure specialist AI agents for research, outreach, lead qualification and support, connected to company tools.
why_choose: Its Invent assistant helps identify processes to automate and turns them into agents.
how_to_start: Contact sales; the pricing page showed only an enterprise offer during the check.

name: Dify
short_description: Open-source platform for building agentic workflows and LLM apps.
long_description: Dify is a platform to build AI agents, RAG knowledge pipelines and LLM workflows on a visual canvas, then deploy them as apps or APIs. It is open source and can run on Dify Cloud, in a private VPC or self-hosted, which makes it popular with technical teams. A free plan is available on the cloud, with paid plans for more message credits and team members.
use_cases: Build agentic workflows;RAG knowledge pipelines;Self-host LLM apps
use_case: Build agentic workflows and RAG knowledge pipelines on a visual canvas, and deploy them as apps or APIs.
why_choose: It is open source and can run on Dify Cloud, in a private VPC or self-hosted.
how_to_start: Self-host the Community Edition with Docker, or choose Get Started on the free Sandbox plan (200 message credits).

name: Langflow
short_description: Open-source visual builder for AI agents, RAG pipelines and MCP servers.
long_description: Langflow is an open-source, Python-based tool for building AI agents and workflows with a visual editor. Components for models, vector stores and tools are connected on a canvas, and each flow can be served as an API or exposed as an MCP server. It can be self-hosted, and the site also offers a free cloud account for deployment. Professional services and premier support are offered by the company behind it.
use_cases: Prototype AI agents visually;Build RAG flows
use_case: Assemble AI agents and RAG flows from models, vector stores and tools on a visual canvas, then serve them as an API or MCP server.
why_choose: It is open source and Python-based, and each flow can be exposed as an API or MCP server.
how_to_start: Download the open-source builder to run it yourself, or choose Get Started for Free on the cloud.

name: Bardeen
short_description: Browser-based web scraper and enrichment tool for finding and qualifying sales leads.
long_description: Bardeen is a lead sourcing tool built around an AI web scraper. Users extract data from websites, enrich contacts with emails and phone numbers, score leads with AI and sync results to spreadsheets or CRMs. Pricing is credit-based: every account keeps 100 free credits, and paid plans start at $10 per month, with larger plans at $50 per month and custom bulk credits on request.
use_cases: Scrape and enrich leads;Automate browser tasks
use_case: Scrape websites for leads, enrich contacts with emails and phone numbers, score them with AI and sync them to a spreadsheet or CRM.
why_choose: It focuses on browser-based lead sourcing rather than general app integration.
how_to_start: Choose Get started; every account has 100 free credits. Run the AI web scraper on a target site.

name: Browser Use
short_description: Cloud browsers and web agents for automating tasks on websites, with an open-source library.
long_description: Browser Use offers infrastructure for agents that operate websites. Its hosted agents complete tasks in a browser, and its cloud browsers can be driven by a developer's own agent. The project started as an open-source library. Pricing is pay-as-you-go with no subscription: cloud browsers cost $0.02 per hour, residential proxies $5 per GB, and new accounts get $1 of free credit. The company lists SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliance.
use_cases: Automate website tasks with AI agents;Run cloud browsers
use_case: Have hosted AI agents complete website tasks such as forms, logins or data extraction, or drive cloud browsers from your own agent.
why_choose: It started as an open-source library, offers pay-as-you-go pricing with no subscription, and supports Playwright or Puppeteer over CDP.
how_to_start: Start for free with $1 of credit, then run a hosted agent task or connect your agent to a cloud browser.

name: Skyvern
short_description: Open-source browser automation that uses AI to fill forms, log in and extract data across websites.
long_description: Skyvern automates repetitive browser work such as logging into portals, filling forms, downloading invoices and extracting data. It uses AI to read pages, so it does not rely on fixed selectors that break when sites change. The core is open source. The hosted service has a free plan with 5,000 credits per month, a Hobby plan at $29 per month and a Pro plan at $149 per month; it supports 2FA and lists HIPAA and SOC 2 compliance.
use_cases: Automate form filling and logins;Extract web data
use_case: Automate portal logins, form filling, invoice downloads and data extraction, including sites that require 2FA.
why_choose: It reads pages with AI instead of fixed selectors, which break when sites change, and its core is open source.
how_to_start: Use the hosted free plan (5,000 credits/mo) and choose Start Building, or run the open-source core yourself.
